audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart reads Galio x4 then Skill x3; the packet and the content layer both read Galio x5 then Aurelion Sol x2. Rows 5 and 6 belong to Aurelion Sol on range — 750 beam against a 650 Justice Punch. 49.29% over 637 games is even, so 7/10 was a shade harsh.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Galio's PASSIVE a shield — content early says 'Galio's shield passive', wants.foe[0] says 'behind his passive shield', spikes[0] says 'his magic shield absorbs'.
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash: 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area.' It is an auto-attack reset with AoE, not a shield. The shields come from Shield of Durand (W) and Hero's Entrance (R). A reader who believes the passive shields will play the whole lane around a mechanic that does not exist.
audit.corrected: early, wants.foe[0], whys[0] and spikes[0].text rewritten to name Colossal Smash correctly and put the shield where it belongs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield of Durand's taunt was never mentioned anywhere on the page, and neither was the fact that either of his CC abilities cancels an Aurelion Sol channel.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies' — hardCC at 275 range on 18s at rank 1. Both Breath of Light and Astral Flight carry the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'). So the real combo is Justice Punch knockup at 650 into a taunt at 275, and the beam ends on the first of the two.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, enemyWin, tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, spikes[0].text, early and late now state it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of the four missingInteractions entries for this matchup are derived from misfiring tooltip flags and must NOT be written to the page: 'Your Astral Flight (W) shuts off Galio's Justice Punch (E)' and 'Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E)'.
audit.why: Both rest on terrain flags that contradict Riot's own text. ownerKit W says 'Aurelion Sol flies OVER terrain in a targeted direction' — he traverses terrain, he does not create it, so it grounds nothing. enemyKit E says 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters' — a dash and a knockup, no wall. Per the brief's own rule, when a derived flag contradicts the description, the description wins.
audit.corrected: Neither claim was written. The two valid entries (your-channel-punished, autoreset-burst-tell) were both added.

notes: IMPORTANT — two of the four missingInteractions entries supplied for this matchup are FALSE and I deliberately did not write them. Both come from terrain flags that contradict Riot's text: (1) 'Your Astral Flight (W) shuts off Galio's Justice Punch (E)' — Aurelion Sol's W says he 'flies OVER terrain', he does not create any, so it grounds nothing; (2) 'Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E)' — his E is a dash plus knockup with no wall in the description. If the flag generator is fixable, those two rules are producing bad advice across every Aurelion Sol matchup, not just this one. The packet's two suspectNames are both false positives (Hero's Entrance and Justice Punch are correct names). Row 4 of the chart was a genuine judgement call: the full layer's why said Aurelion Sol gains at 6 and the content why said Galio does. I sided with the packet and the content layer — Hero's Entrance is global and Falling Star is not — and rewrote phases[4].why in the same proposal so the row and its sentence agree.
